spec: AES MixColumns (forward), a 32x32 GF(2) linear map. Column matrix [[2,3,1,1],[1,2,3,1],[1,1,2,3],[3,1,1,2]] over GF(2^8) with reduction polynomial 0x11b.
note: sha256_circuit_json is over the exact circuit JSON file bytes as written. sha256_canonical_gates is SHA-256 over the exact UTF-8 bytes of the compact JSON string {"inputCount":32,"gates":[...]} with keys in that order; reproduce it with scripts/reproduce_canonical_hashes.py.

circuits.outputConvention: output j (j in 0..31) is MixColumns output bit j; bit j = bit (j mod 8) of state byte (j div 8), least-significant-bit-first within each byte. It is produced at internal signal index outputSignals[j].

verified.method: checked against AES MixColumns rebuilt from GF(2^8) in verify.py, and against 32 basis-vector responses in the Verilog testbench

circuits.claim: Uses fewer 2-input XOR gates than the 99-gate depth-3 AES MixColumns point reported by Shi, Feng, and Xu (ToSC 2023). Depth 3 is the known minimum depth for this map (an output depending on w inputs needs depth at least ceil(log2(w)), and MixColumns has outputs of weight 7); we do not make an optimality claim on the gate count.

circuits.provenance: Found by this project's own search from scratch, with no imported material anywhere in the chain: fleet worker c_naive, restart 18, rooted in randomized balanced XOR trees over the 32 raw inputs (root naive#2163, no seeded circuit), then root -> 89 gates -> 88 gates at depth 7 at walk iteration 37270 (worker run-time t = 68238.2 s, 2026-07-28 17:19:45 -0400) -> this 88 at depth 6 at walk iteration 37501 (t = 68238.7 s, 2026-07-28 17:19:45 -0400), 0.5 s later by the walk's Pareto depth tie-break. All wall-clock times here are local, UTC-04:00, not UTC; the worker process these run-times are measured from started 2026-07-27 22:22:27 -0400, so t is 18.96 h at the find. Why nothing imported can be in that chain, strongest fact first: the ROOT reads nothing. The worker's root spec was constructor:naive, and the constructor branch of the archived worker's root generator calls only constructors.build(name, seed) -- it has no file-reading path at all, and every branch of that generator that can open a circuit off disk is a different branch, unreachable under this spec. All 38 restarts logged in the session that produced this circuit opened on a naive#<seed> root, and root naive#2163 rebuilds to exactly the logged 139 gates at depth 3. The remaining routes were audited closed as well, and are stated as two-part arguments because the fleet launcher as run is not archived: the hunt worker never mentions the cross-pollination knob (pop_glob) anywhere AND its untouched log contains none of the lines the engine emits when a merge brings material in; family repulsion was off; and a per-restart local context means no global-best carryover. Knobs alone would not settle it -- the derived 88 at depth 5 in this file had identical knobs and imported material still reached it, through its root. This is the first 88 this project has found from scratch; the 88 at depth 7 remains its independently found match of Jean's published point. Found in campaign 87, hunt87 fleet (slp-plateau-search v3.0.0). circuits.claim: Realizes AES MixColumns in 88 two-input XOR gates at depth 6. This is NOT a new gate-count record: 88 is the existing best-known count, published by Jean (ePrint 2026/1481, posted 2026-07-23, who has priority) and independently matched by mixcolumns_88gates_depth7 in this repository. What this circuit does is improve the published depth-count Pareto frontier at its depth: it dominates Jean's 88 (equal count, one level shallower - with the standing caveat that depth 7 is this project's own measurement of its own transcription, because that paper states no depth), and it uses four fewer gates than the published depth-6 point (92: Maximov, ePrint 2019/833; also Xiang et al., ToSC 2020(2), s-XOR). It is a construction distinct from every other circuit here: its highest internal-mask overlap with any of them is 47 masks (Jaccard 0.362, against the superseded mixcolumns_89gates_depth10; the highest against any 88 here is 43 masks, Jaccard 0.323). 87 was not found, and no optimality claim is made.
